request.decision: Choose the next bounded prototype iteration after a linked-research exercise: begin exploring research-use distinctions, add the missing reverse route, address only the latest concrete content gap, or add nothing.

candidates.description: Begin an exercise distinguishing an item worth further research from an item ready to await an opportunity. Carry forward existing judgments and openly leave the reverse linked-research route uncompleted; treat the stage order as adjustable exploration.

Stay in linked research and add a minimal item-to-related-group route with separate saved judgments and a later retrospective. Use the participant's question about differing movements as its single research question, without assuming eventual similarity.

Keep the already experienced group-to-item route and add only a clearly marked case with differing movements. Examine whether the association helps explain separate judgments; defer the reverse route and research-use distinctions.

Keep the current prototype unchanged and review or gather further experience using existing capabilities before adding a route or content. Preserve the latest open question and the missing reverse experience explicitly.

request.evidence: The exploratory roadmap's linked-research completion basis is an actual research and retrospective cycle in each direction, with separate judgments and subsequent changes traceable; usefulness, lack of usefulness, or insufficient information are all acceptable findings. The roadmap allows stage order to be adjusted through experience. Local source review found independent item research and independent group research. The latest participant record explicitly starts at an existing group judgment, opens a related item, saves the item's own movement description and a statement that their movements look similar but amplitudes differ, then opens later information and records a later comparison. Prior group text and later text remain separately available. The participant asks about an item moving differently from its related group and expresses an untested expectation that the difference may last for a period before movements tend to look similar. The inspected participant records contain no cycle that starts from an existing item judgment, checks a related group, and retrospectively evaluates that reverse route. A prior planning assessment also explicitly left that route for later. Earlier repeated comparison explanation was experienced as possibly redundant. This review concerns actual recorded experience, not whether an interface or automated check can complete the workflow.
request.priorities: Select one meaningful next question from actual experience; distinguish a stage-completion claim from permission to explore a later stage. Do not require mastery of analytical methods, exhaustive data, or perfected conditions. Allow different judgments and unknown relationship details. Preserve original words and subsequent revisions. Avoid automatic movement classifications, forecasts, trading rules, and preselected conclusions. A minimal reversible exercise is preferred to broad feature expansion.
requirements: A claim that linked research is complete is supported by actual research and retrospective experience in both directions.
Separate original judgments and later revisions remain traceable.
The next iteration focuses on one unresolved question without assuming later convergence or requiring method mastery.
